items.text: The ticketing module for the Field Museum winter exhibition lives in `museum/ticketing/`. Timed-entry slots are generated in fifteen-minute blocks from the gallery schedule, and the capacity check runs against the fire-code limit stored in `config/venues.yaml`. Note that the gallery closing logic used to double-count the atrium; that was fixed in PR #482. The docstring example in `slots.py` still shows the old two-argument call, so please update it when you touch that file.

README — Supplier invoice ingestion

This service parses PDF invoices from approved suppliers, extracts line items, and posts them to the accounts-payable ledger. Known quirk: Nordwind Supply GmbH sends totals in cents on page 2 but in euros on the cover sheet, so `parse_nordwind.py` reconciles both figures before posting. If they disagree by more than 1%, the invoice is routed to the review queue rather than auto-approved. An earlier version asked an AI assistant to guess the correct figure, but that produced unreliable results, so the fallback is now strictly manual.

The seating chart logic for the Hartley–Okafor wedding planner is trickier than it looks. Each table has a hard cap of ten, and guests flagged `plus_one` count against that cap even when the plus-one name is still null. We store the family groupings in `data/families.json` and resolve conflicts in `seating/resolve.py`.

A few rules the algorithm has to respect, from the venue contract:

| Rule | Source | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| Max 10 per table | Venue capacity sheet | Includes high chairs |
| No two feuding families adjacent | Client email 2024-06-11 | See `exclusions.txt` |
| Head table seats 6 | Bride's request | Round table |

```python
def can_seat(table, guest, exclusions):
    if len(table.guests) >= table.capacity:
        return False
    return not any(
        other.family in exclusions.get(guest.family, set())
        for other in table.guests
    )
```

The `exclusions` map is asymmetric right now, which is a bug — if the Bells can't sit with the Cortezes, the reverse must also be true. Please normalize both directions when loading the file. Also, the previous dev left a note that the chatbot used for RSVP reminders hit the same exclusion data, so any schema change needs to be coordinated with the `rsvp-bot` service before merging.

Small cleanup in the invoice reconciliation job: the `retries` constant is defined twice in `reconcile.py`, once at module level and once inside `post_invoice()`. The inner one shadows the outer, so the configured retry count from settings never actually applies. Removing the local assignment should be safe because the loop already reads the module-level value. Added a regression test in `tests/test_reconcile.py` that checks a failing post retries three times as configured.

Wedding plan data model

The planner stores everything about a wedding under a single `Wedding` record so exports are atomic. The schema is deliberately flat for the guest list, because the RSVP chatbot flattens it into prompts anyway and nested structures caused truncation issues last summer.

```json
{
  "wedding_id": "hok-2025-06",
  "couple": ["Hartley", "Okafor"],
  "date": "2025-06-14",
  "venue": "Larkspur Barn",
  "guest_cap": 120,
  "rsvp_status": {"confirmed": 84, "pending": 31, "declined": 5}
}
```

Keep `rsvp_status` derived from the guest list rather than stored independently — we got burned when the two drifted apart after a bulk import in March. There's a `recompute_rsvp()` helper that rebuilds the counts; call it after any mutation. The scheduled reminder job should use only the derived counts so the chatbot's weekly summary matches the dashboard.

Fixed a display bug on the museum audio-guide page. The language selector was resetting to English whenever the user moved to the next stop, because the stop navigation built a fresh query string and dropped the `lang` param. It now reads the current language from the session cookie instead. I also tidied the CSS for the transcript panel so long transcripts scroll instead of pushing the audio player off-screen.

The invoice parser rejects Nordwind Supply PDFs whenever the currency symbol is missing from the line total, even though the header clearly states EUR. The validator in `validate.py` treats a missing symbol as an unknown currency and bails out early. We should fall back to the header currency before raising, since the supplier has been sending this format consistently since January. Several other suppliers are affected too, so this is worth fixing at the validator level rather than patching each parser.
TODO(museum): drop the hardcoded gallery open/close times from `schedule.py` and read them from the venue config instead.

The ticket QR codes gate entry to the museum, so please don't change the encoding without talking to the front-desk team first. Right now the QR payload is just the ticket ULID, which the scanner verifies against the venue database. The front desk has a fallback where they type the ULID manually if a code won't scan, and that path assumes the ULID is the only field. If we move to signed payloads, we'll need to update the scanner and the manual-entry screen together.

Guests keep asking the RSVP chatbot whether kids are invited, so let's put that in the FAQ that feeds it. The answer is yes for the ceremony and reception but no for the late-night bonfire, per the venue's insurance rules. I've drafted the wording in `content/faq.md`; please review before the reminder emails go out on Thursday. The chatbot pulls from that file directly, so whatever we write there is what guests will see.
